**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

- **Exclusivity runs in our favour only.** Section 3.19 ("Exclusivity Commitment of SFJ") plus the "Exclusive Period" definition (1.1.68 — clinical trials to 21 Nov 2022; sale/offer for sale to 21 Nov 2024) restrict SFJ and its Affiliates from Competing Product activity. Per the detection guidance, exclusivity granted to the Customer is acceptable and not flagged.
- **No sole-supplier lock-in on PB.** Sections 2.4.1–2.4.3 permit each Party, including PB, to use any CRO listed on Exhibit B or approved by the JDC and to contract with any Approved Vendor for services, equipment, materials and supplies; PB is itself the GMP Manufacturer under Section 3.14.1.1, directly or through an Approved CRO. The JDC approval gate is mutual and process-based, not an exclusive-dealing commitment.
- **Article 7 covenants are out of scope.** The Section 7.5.5 Licensing Transaction consent gate, plus 7.5.3/7.5.6/7.5.7, are financing-style negative covenants over PB Intellectual Property and royalty streams (with an Excluded Licensing Transaction carve-out and an expedited arbitration test on "Material Impact"). They constrain licensing/encumbrance, not procurement, so they belong to the financing-covenant rule rather than being double-flagged here.

Result: the document sits at the **preferred** position — no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binding PB.
